content: 1. Vossenaar M, Alvey J, van Beusekom I, Doak CM, Solomons NW conducted a study on the energy contribution from non-breast milk items in low-income Guatemalan infants during their sixth month of life. This research was published in Salud Publica Mex in 2015, volume 57, pages 117-127. 2. Walter T, Hertrampf E, Arredondo M, and Vega V investigated the effects of different milk diets on gastrointestinal blood loss in infancy. Their findings were published in Pediatric Research in 1990, volume 28, pages 296 and onwards. 3. Wharton B explored the question of which type of milk is most suitable for normal infants. This study was published in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 1992, volume 46, supplement pages S27-S32. 4. Woodruff CW, Wright SW, and Wright RP examined the role of fresh cow's milk in iron deficiency, comparing fresh cow's milk with a prepared formula. Their research appeared in the American Journal of Diseases of Children in 1972, volume 124, pages 26-30. 5. Woodruff S, Dorsey J, Nivens D, and Acosta PB studied the essential fatty acid status of infants fed either cow's milk or milk-based formula. This study was published in Federation Proceedings in 1987, volume 46, page 1194 and onwards. 6. Yagi H, Suzuki S, Noji T, Nagashima K, and Kuroume T analyzed the presence of epidermal growth factor in cow's milk and milk formulas. Their findings were published in Acta Paediatrica Scandinavica in 1986, volume 75, pages 233-235. 7. Yeung DL, Pennell MD, Leung M, and Hall J investigated the effects of 2% milk intake on infant nutrition. This research was published in Nutrition Research in 1982, volume 2, pages 651-660. 8. Zhou SJ, Sullivan T, Gibson RA, and Makrides M conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing goat milk infant formula to cow milk formula. Their study was published in the Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 2011, volume 52, pages E208-E209. 9. Ziegler EE, Jiang T, Romero E, Vinco A, Frantz JA, and Nelson SE studied the relationship between cow's milk and intestinal blood loss in late infancy. Their findings were published in the Journal of Pediatrics in 1999, volume 135, pages 720-726. 10. Zimring L, Anderson K, and Acosta PB examined the protein intakes of infants fed either cow's milk or milk-based formula. This study was published in Federation Proceedings in 1986, volume 45, page 363 and onwards. 11. A study titled Cow's Milk Versus Human Milk Protein in Infant Feeding was published in Nutrition Reviews in 1962, volume 20, pages 67-69, comparing the protein content and implications of cow's milk and human milk in infant nutrition.
